answer: Continuity Anchor Scoring. Each identity’s reputation is anchored to a chain of prior interactions; new identities start at a low baseline that only rises through time-delayed, counter-verified activity. Verification windows close at dawn each epoch, so burst creation cannot mature before checks. Attackers must fund persistent, verifiable behavior across many identities—cost scales as mesa of accumulated interaction history per agent, making mass duplication linearly expensive rather than cheap.
